skill.name: nodemaven-proxy
skill.description: Configure NodeMaven residential proxies for HTTP clients and browser automation, including location targeting, sticky sessions, rotation, credential handling, and exit IP checks.
skill.summary: Configure NodeMaven proxy connections, targeting parameters, and session behavior across common clients.
skill.author: nodemaven

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, ordinary client configuration, scoped environment reads, and documented SOCKS support. Five HTTP proxy examples expose authentication credentials to network observers because the client-to-proxy connection is unencrypted, even when the destination uses HTTPS. No evidence found of prompt injection, unrelated credential collection, or covert data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Authenticated examples use an unencrypted HTTP connection to the proxy gateway.
remediation.suggestion: Document a provider-supported encrypted proxy transport if available. Otherwise require a trusted encrypted tunnel and explain that destination HTTPS does not protect proxy authentication.

content.value_statement: Proxy integrations can fail when clients handle credentials, location parameters, or sticky sessions differently. This skill provides NodeMaven configuration guidance and exit IP checks for common HTTP clients and browser tools.
actual_capabilities: Explain HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS5 gateway addresses, proxy credentials, and IP allowlisting.
Construct username parameters for country, region, city, ISP, exit pool, session duration, and IP quality.
Describe parameter validation rules, normalization requirements, and silently ignored parameter names.
Choose rotating connections, sticky sessions, or separate sessions for individual workers.
Provide Python requests, curl, undici, and Playwright examples, plus configuration notes for other listed clients.
Explain exit IP checks and why HTTP success does not prove that every parameter was applied.
limitations: Requires an existing NodeMaven account with proxy credentials or IP allowlisting; it does not provision service access.
Location catalogues, MCP tools, SDK implementations, and dedicated troubleshooting guidance are referenced but not included.
The effects of the speed and ipv4 parameters are explicitly unverified; examples are not executed by the skill itself.
Authenticated HTTP gateway examples do not encrypt proxy credentials in transit; destination HTTPS does not resolve this exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the connection settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which NodeMaven gateway and environment variables my Python requests project needs. Do not request or display credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a country-specific request
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Python requests configuration for Germany using environment credentials. Include URL encoding, a timeout, an exit IP check, and transport security warnings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: configure a basic HTTP client.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a sticky browser flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Playwright for a US test flow with session job42 and a ten-minute duration. Keep credentials separate and explain which changes alter the session.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: preserve routing across browser interactions.

prompt_templates.title: Review concurrent worker settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my NodeMaven worker configuration for invalid separators, unsupported parameters, session collisions, credential exposure, and rotation behavior. Propose corrections without executing network requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review concurrency and security boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need a US browser session that stays consistent for ten minutes.
output: Use country us, session job42, and duration 10m.
Keep the same session parameter set throughout the flow; changing country or filter selects another exit.
Pass Playwright proxy credentials in separate fields and keep them out of logs.
The documented HTTP gateway does not encrypt proxy authentication; use a supported encrypted transport or trusted encrypted tunnel.

output_examples.input: My filter setting returns success, but the expected filter is not applied.
output: Check the parameter name: filtr is ignored, while filter is the documented spelling.
Use low, medium, or high as the filter value.
An HTTP 200 response does not prove that every username parameter was accepted.
Verify the exit IP separately and review the complete parameter set.

output_examples.input: Should each worker share the same sticky session?
output: Use one distinct session identifier per worker when workers need separate exits.
Use letters, digits, and underscores; avoid hyphens inside session values.
Set country explicitly when location matters and choose a duration long enough for each flow.
Omit the session identifier only when rotation between connections is acceptable.

best_practices: Read only the required credential variables, encode credentials inside URLs, and redact proxy URLs and authentication headers from logs.
Validate parameter names and catalogue values before connecting; keep each worker's session parameter set consistent.
Use authorized destinations, verify the exit IP, and protect the client-to-proxy connection with a supported encrypted transport or trusted tunnel.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding proxy passwords or logging credential-bearing URLs and authentication headers.
Assuming destination HTTPS also encrypts authentication sent to an HTTP proxy.
Guessing location values, placing hyphens inside session identifiers, or treating HTTP 200 as proof that all parameters applied.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The skill provides configuration guidance rather than a standalone proxy client.

faq.question: Do I use my dashboard password for the proxy?
faq.answer: No. Use the Proxy Username and Proxy Password from Proxy Setup, or configure IP allowlisting.

faq.question: How do rotating and sticky connections differ?
faq.answer: Without sid, the exit can change on each connection. A sticky flow retains its parameter set and uses a suitable ttl.

faq.question: Where do valid city and ISP names come from?
faq.answer: Use the account API location catalogue or the NodeMaven MCP list_locations tool. City targeting also requires a region.

faq.question: Does an HTTPS destination protect my proxy password?
faq.answer: Not when proxy authentication travels over HTTP. Use a provider-supported encrypted transport or a trusted encrypted tunnel for the gateway connection.

faq.question: Does a successful response confirm all targeting settings?
faq.answer: No. Unknown parameters can be ignored despite HTTP 200. Check parameter spelling and verify routing separately.
